subject: Tenant audit & access log export windows — boundary, retention, and deletion workflows
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Export windows + retention boundary questions for Acme tenant

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow ups from compliance as we prepare our evidence package: can you confirm the exact export window for audit/access logs? We need to know: 1) earliest possible time-range we can request a bulk export for (eg last 90 days vs 365), 2) whether exports include masked PII by default, and 3) which regional datastore the export is pulled from when we request exports for our EU-backed patients (we're US region but some records are residency-bound).

Also, if we request a bulk export and then later ask for deletion, what guarantees exist around tombstone/erase propagation and timelines? Our legal team wants a single-step attestation we can hand to regulators.

If it helps I've attached a quick CSV with the list of audit types we need (login, config-change, model-invoke).

Appreciate the details — Emily
Compliance Manager, Acme Health

Attachment: audit_export_request.csv (1 row sample)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Emily Park <emily.park@acmehealth.com>; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Export windows + retention boundary questions for Acme tenant

Emily — thanks for the clear list, and good questions. Short answers up front:
- Export window: we support ad-hoc exports covering up to 730 days historically for audit logs; for access logs the practical window is 365 days via the self-serve tool. Longer-term snapshots can be produced by request (operations SLA applies).
- PII handling: exports are produced with the same masking policy as tenant views by default; we can provide a raw (unmasked) export under an approved legal/contractual process and KMS audit (requires customer-signed access attestation).
- Region: the export origin follows the tenant's residency config. For mixed-residency accounts we shard exports by data residency and provide a manifest that maps files to regions.

On deletion/attestation: when a customer requests a delete of tenant data we run a multi-stage erase: tombstone -> background purge -> index rebuild. We can provide an erase attestation that lists export manifests, purge job IDs, and timestamps. Standard delete propagation is 30 days end-to-end for indexed access traces; for archived segments it can be up to 90 days depending on shard rebuild schedules.

I'm attaching a short instructions CSV (audit_export_instructions_v2.csv) that shows endpoints and required fields for a standard export job. Marissa / Rishi — can you add any operational caveats?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Product Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: audit_export_instructions_v2.csv
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Emily Park <emily.park@acmehealth.com>; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Export windows + retention boundary questions for Acme tenant

Emily — quick operational notes:
- Format & delivery: exports delivered as gzipped Parquet + manifest. We can alternatively push to a customer S3/GCS bucket (pre-authorised) or provide a signed temporary download link. Delivery SLA for ad-hoc exports is 48-72 hours for <90 day windows, and 5 business days for larger/archival pulls.
- Retention boundaries: tenant-level retention config governs live retention; audit/access logs are indexed with a separate TTL which defaults to 365 days but is configurable for Dedicated/Private customers. For Hosted tenants the 365 default is standard unless there's a contract clause.
- Deletion timeline caveat: if the tenant has active legal holds (we track via the legal-hold API) we block purge jobs until release. We include legal-hold flags in the export manifest so customers see the freeze scope.

Also, small FYI: when we produce cross-region manifests we include checksum and region tags so your internal evidence team can show provenance.

—Marissa
Senior Operations PM, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Park <emily.park@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Export windows + retention boundary questions for Acme tenant

Thanks — that's helpful. Two follow-ups from legal: 1) can you confirm the exact fields included in the manifest (we need audit ids, shard-region, checksum, and whether the record was masked), and 2) what attestation language can you supply for the erase confirmation? Our regulator requires a signed statement from the vendor with a job-level ID and timestamp.

We'll also need the export files delivered to our pre-authorised S3 bucket (US-East). Please confirm that delivery option and the expected URL format so our security team can whitelist.

Emily
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Emily Park <emily.park@acmehealth.com>; monica_patel@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Export windows + retention boundary questions for Acme tenant

Emily — follow up with the precise operational commitments we can make:
1) Manifest fields: export_manifest.json contains file_name, start_ts, end_ts, tenant_id, region, checksum_sha256, masked: boolean, record_count, purge_job_id (if deletion requested). We'll include a sample manifest with the export.
2) Erase attestation: we provide a PDF attestation signed by Redwood's security lead. It will reference the purge_job_id, job start/end timestamps, affected index ranges, and a short description of the purge steps. For high-assurance requests (e.g., regulator-driven), we can include an ingress map showing which datastores and archival shards were touched.
3) S3 delivery: yes — we can deliver to a pre-authorised S3 bucket via a temporary put with bucket ACL pre-flight. Expected path format: s3://acme-audit-exports/YYYYMMDD/tenant-<tenant_id>/export-<jobid>.parquet.gz. We'll coordinate an IAM role for cross-account delivery.

Next steps: I'll open an operational ticket (HS-82754) to track the export and attach the sample manifest & attestation template. Monica — can your team run the export schedule and confirm the 72-hour window for the initial <90d> export?

-Rishi
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachment: evidence_manifest_acme.zip (contains sample manifest & attestation template)
